passages.title: Should Public Parks Allow Food Trucks

conversation.name: Speaker A
conversation.text: I think allowing food trucks in parks would make them more lively. People could grab a snack while spending time outdoors.

conversation.name: Speaker B
conversation.text: Maybe, but wouldn’t it create more litter? Not everyone cleans up after themselves.

conversation.name: Speaker A
conversation.text: True, but the city could install more trash bins and hire cleaners. The added convenience could bring more people to the parks.

conversation.name: Speaker B
conversation.text: I still think it could spoil the natural atmosphere. Parks are meant to be green spaces, not outdoor food courts.

choices.text: They will reduce noise in the park
They will make parks more lively
They will attract professional chefs
They will reduce traffic around parks

questions.question: What is one concern raised about this idea?

choices.text: It will be too expensive for food vendorsy
It may increase litter
It could attract too many tourists

passages.title: Should Schools Start Later in the Morning?

conversation.name: Speaker A
conversation.text: I believe schools should start later. Teenagers need more sleep, and studies show it helps them perform better.

conversation.name: Speaker B
conversation.text: That sounds good in theory, but it could cause issues for working parents. They rely on early school hours to get to work on time.

conversation.name: Speaker A
conversation.text: Still, if students are healthier and more focused, isn’t it worth it?

conversation.name: Speaker B
conversation.text: It’s hard to say. It might just shift the problem elsewhere, like after-school care.

questions.question: What benefit is mentioned for starting school later?

choices.text: It allows teachers more time to prepare
It helps students get more sleep
It reduces transportation costs
It shortens the school day

questions.question: What is one concern about starting school later?

choices.text: It might reduce the quality of lessons
It could cause scheduling problems for parents
It will reduce student enrollment
It could increase transportation accidents

conversation.name: Speaker A
conversation.text: SI fully support banning single-use plastics. They’re terrible for the environment and clog up our oceans.

conversation.name: Speaker B
conversation.text: I agree they’re a problem, but banning them could hurt small businesses that rely on cheap packaging.

conversation.name: Speaker A
conversation.text: There are affordable alternatives now, like paper or compostable materials.

conversation.name: Speaker B
conversation.text: Yes, but switching takes time and money. Some businesses might struggle during the transition.
